subject: maths
question: Kajal offers two successive discounts of 10% and 8% on the sale of a cosmetic item to her customer. What is the equivalent single percentage discount offered by Kajal?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equivalent Discount = [x + y − (x × y ÷ 100)]%

Substitute x = 10 and y = 8:

Discount % = 10 + 8 − (10 × 8 ÷ 100) = 18 − 0.8 = 17.2%

Convert to decimal form: 17.2 ÷ 100 = 0.172 = 17.2%

**∴ The correct answer is 17.2%. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First discount (d₁) = 10%

Second discount (d₂) = 8%

**Formula Used:**

Final Selling Price = Marked Price × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)

 MP = 100 
• −10% 90 
• −8% SP = 82.8 Equivalent Discount = 100 − 82.8 = 17.2 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Marked Price = 100 units

⇒ Price after 10% discount = 100 − (10/100 × 100) = 90

⇒ Price after 8% additional discount = 90 − (8/100 × 90)

⇒ Price after 8% additional discount = 90 − 7.2 = 82.8

⇒ Total discount amount = 100 − 82.8 = 17.2

⇒ Equivalent single discount percentage = (17.2 ÷ 100) × 100 = 17.2%

⇒ Decimal representation = 17.2 ÷ 100 = 0.172

**∴ The correct answer is 0.172.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Three Successive Discounts

For three discounts a%, b%, and c%, the final price is MP × (1−a/100) × (1−b/100) × (1−c/100).

Net Percentage Change

The net change for two successive percentage changes x and y is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Discount and Marked Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), while Profit or Loss is usually calculated on the Cost Price (CP).
